_doc: Variable registry for /new-project - the single home of every value a new chip project must define before the verification flow starts.
Read by new_project.py (detect/status/set/apply/check) and by the new-project skill (interview).
A new framework variable (a new flow_env.sh setting, a new config knob, a new filelist) is registered here in the same change (arch_memory R7).
Paths in 'file'/'files' are relative to verify/. 'kind' decides how apply writes the value:
json_field     top-level key of a JSON file ('key'); 'type' bool|str
sh_var         VAR="value" line in a shell file ('var'); relative repo paths are prefixed with $database_path/ when 'repo_path' is true
text_file      whole file rendered from 'template' ({v} = value)
filelist_block lines between 'start' and 'end' marker comments, one per list item, rendered from 'line' ({v})
choice_rewrite per-choice literal snippets ('snippets': {file: {choice: text}}) swapped in the listed files
record_only    kept in answers.json only (drives the report / later stages)
detect_only    never written; check verifies the tool/setting on this machine (machine-level, CLAUDE.md rule)
'rewrites': [{files, pattern}] - after apply, every occurrence of pattern with the previously applied value is replaced by the new value.
'deferrable': the user may answer 'defer'; the item is listed as pending in the check report.
'phase': interview order (1 identity, 2 inputs, 3 machine tools, 4 VCS server, 5 filelists, 6 Claude config).

vars.prompt: Chip/project name (lower-case identifier). Names the system top tb_top_<name>.sv and its filelist.
Project id (deployed as sim/project_name; read by wsim, the Makefile and testjson2lst).
Does the chip have a register model (top-level enable_ral)? false forces every module enable_ral=false and adapter_type="".
Generate the top-level interface config (env/top_if.sv + top_if_pc.sv)?
Directory with the architecture/design/verification-plan documents (repo-root relative). 'none' = pre-research mode on reference RTL.
Directory holding the chip RTL (repo-root relative), scanned to propose the RTL filelist.
Register-table CSV consumed by RalGen (repo-root relative or absolute). Needed only when enable_ral is on.
UVM-1.2 library for the oEDA flow (environment variable UVM_HOME, default $HOME/tools/uvm-1.2).
Verilator on PATH for the oEDA flow (OSS CAD Suite environment sourced).
Synopsys VCS on PATH (VCS sign-off flow).
VERDI_HOME (FSDB dump / Verdi GUI).
Where does the oEDA (Verilator) flow run? linux = natively on this Linux host; wsl = WSL2 on a Windows box.

CLAUDE.md.wsl: Local fast-iteration flow on this Windows box, inside WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04: Verilator (OSS CAD Suite) + UVM-1.2 + FST waves + `verilator_coverage`. Machine setup, the Surfer viewer and `wsl.exe` invocation pitfalls: `docs/ops/oeda_local_setup.md`.
CLAUDE.md.linux: Local fast-iteration flow, run natively on this Linux host: Verilator (OSS CAD Suite) + UVM-1.2 + FST waves + `verilator_coverage`. Machine setup and the waveform viewer: `docs/ops/oeda_local_setup.md`.

vars.prompt: Python 3 (with openpyxl) used by RalGen, testjson2lst and the Makefile seed.
Dispatch simulations through LSF (bsub)? FALSE runs every case on the local host.
Default LSF queue (also the pattern used to discover sibling queues in the hosts file).
LSF cluster hosts file (lsb.hosts) read for queue/host slot discovery.
Host-name fragments (3rd '-'-separated field of $HOST) allowed to submit to LSF, space separated; empty = any host.
Extended regex matching execution-host names in the hosts file.
sed expression mapping a host-group name in the hosts file to its LSF queue name ('s/x/x/' = identity).
DPO learn/apply/reference database root (only used with -dpo).
Chip RTL source files (repo-root relative), in compile order.
RTL include directories (repo-root relative). Empty list = none.
IP model files (repo-root relative). Empty list = none.
Language of conversational output (replies, reports, questions) of the leader and every agent.
Language of every file written into the project (docs, memories, reports, commit messages).
